QUOTE: Struct fields are declared as `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)`, so by default a field `foo` is actually named `private_foo`. Code outside the library that writes `ctx->foo` fails to compile... It is a compile-time guard, not an access-control mechanism.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that the enforcement is a compile-time name mangling (`foo` becomes `private_foo`), a guard rather than access control. That matches the item's "breaking the member name" mechanism. It never says outright that the layout stays visible, but the name-mangling explanation carries the substance.
